section_summary: This section chiefly documents State Department and Army processing of applications for entry into occupied Japan by foreign businessmen, missionaries, and officials, including military permits, theater clearances, and exit-permit waivers. Major cases concern Egyptian merchant Isaac Cohen, Philippine Senator Tomas V. Confesor, Pakistani trader Hussain H. Ahmed, and numerous commercial representatives. The section also contains Commerce Department applicant lists, diplomatic correspondence, application forms, telegrams, internal memoranda, and records-control sheets.

subfiles.title: Commerce-approved commercial representatives, list ending February 12, 1948
subfiles.about: Lists Commerce-approved business representatives seeking entry into Japan from several United States cities.
subfiles.summary: Continuation of a multi-page list naming firms, representatives, citizenship, proposed departure dates, preferred Japan entry periods, and prior approvals. It concludes with Portland, Richmond, San Francisco, and Seattle applicants.

subfiles.title: Supplementary Commerce-approved commercial representatives
subfiles.about: Lists additional business travelers, including Japanese aliens and substitute representatives, proposed for Japan entry.
subfiles.summary: Supplementary list of applicants from Honolulu, Los Angeles, New York, Providence, San Francisco, Houston, and Hempstead. Notes citizenship, desired travel dates, and the substitution of Percy Eugene Allan for Clare Kenneth Viland.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 210 concerning Isaac Cohen's Japan visa
subfiles.about: Forwards Egypt's request for commercial entry clearance to Japan for Isaac Cohen.
subfiles.summary: The embassy invokes American intermediary procedures for countries without representatives in Japan and forwards Egypt's request for Isaac Cohen to exchange Egyptian products for Japanese goods.

subfiles.title: Egyptian Foreign Ministry Note No. 41
subfiles.from: Royal Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Requests referral of Isaac Cohen's Japan visa application to the competent authorities.
subfiles.summary: French-language note supporting Cohen's proposed trade in Egyptian cotton and salt with Japan.

subfiles.title: Translation of Egyptian Foreign Ministry Note No. 41
subfiles.from: Royal Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: English translation of Egypt's request for Isaac Cohen's entry visa.
subfiles.summary: The ministry endorses Cohen's commercial journey and asks the embassy to refer his application to the proper authorities.

subfiles.title: Duplicate of Despatch No. 210 concerning Isaac Cohen
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy forwarding Isaac Cohen's proposed commercial travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reproduces the embassy's request for prompt State Department or SCAP advice on Cohen's application.

subfiles.title: Duplicate French copy of Egyptian Note No. 41
subfiles.from: Royal Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Duplicate French copy endorsing Isaac Cohen's commercial travel.
subfiles.summary: Requests competent-authority consideration of Cohen's Japan entry application for trade in Egyptian cotton and salt.

subfiles.title: Duplicate translation of Egyptian Note No. 41
subfiles.from: Royal Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Duplicate English translation of the Egyptian note supporting Cohen's application.
subfiles.summary: States that Cohen seeks to open commercial business and sell Egyptian cotton and salt in Japan.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting additional information for Joseph Cassuto
subfiles.from: Edmund E. Pendleton Jr., Colbertson, Aitchison & Briggs
subfiles.to: Division of Protective Services, attention Walter F. Chappell
subfiles.about: Forwards Joseph Cassuto's additional information for his Japan and Korea entry application.
subfiles.summary: Counsel transmits Cassuto's letter and offers further data because he hopes to depart as soon as permission is granted.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting Hussain H. Ahmed's military permit
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Reports that the Karachi embassy was informed of Ahmed's theater clearance.
subfiles.summary: Brief permit correspondence concerning Pakistani traveler Hussain H. Ahmed.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on extension of Tomas V. Confesor's permit
subfiles.to: H. C. Corkran, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records authorization to extend Confesor's military permit through May 15.
subfiles.summary: San Francisco's passport agent was authorized to endorse the Army-approved extension.

subfiles.title: Special accommodation for amendment of Confesor's permit
subfiles.about: Explains arrangements for San Francisco to amend Confesor's permit as a special accommodation.
subfiles.summary: The Army approved extension through May 15. Because Confesor was a Philippine citizen in Oakland, the Philippine Embassy arranged for him to visit the San Francisco Passport Agency, which would exceptionally amend his permit.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Confesor's application to the Army
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Forwards Senator Confesor's Japan-entry application and requests prompt notice of the decision.
subfiles.summary: The application was sent following consultation between Army and State officials.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on expedited handling of Confesor's application
subfiles.about: Records Philippine Embassy efforts to expedite Confesor's application before the end of March.
subfiles.summary: Mr. Ruiz delivered a copy by hand and asked for immediate consideration; Mrs. Flickinger agreed special handling could obtain a Tokyo reply before month's end.

subfiles.title: Damaged duplicate of Philippine Embassy note on Confesor
subfiles.about: Fragment asks expedited action on Confesor's application and offers reimbursement.
subfiles.summary: A damaged duplicate preserves only the expense-reimbursement closing; page 419 is essentially blank.

subfiles.title: Philippine Embassy note requesting permission for Confesor
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Senator Confesor to visit Japan briefly on his return to the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Confesor wished to observe Japanese conditions and confer with General MacArthur before flying from Oakland to the Philippines. The embassy offered to reimburse the cost of expediting the request by telegram.

subfiles.title: Application of Tomas V. Confesor for permission to enter Japan
subfiles.from: Tomas V. Confesor, through the Philippine Embassy
subfiles.about: Confesor applies for a ten-day visit to Tokyo and its suburbs.
subfiles.summary: The Filipino senator proposes to fly from the United States in early April to observe conditions and meet General MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Airgram to Karachi reporting Ahmed's theater clearance
subfiles.about: Reports clearance for Hussain H. Ahmed to enter Japan between March 8 and May 5.
subfiles.summary: Ahmed may remain sixty days after entry; the embassy may annotate his passport or provide a certified copy of the airgram.

subfiles.title: Foreign Service file cover, 894.111/3-1548
subfiles.from: Foreign Service of the United States
subfiles.about: Cover sheet for an unclassified travel-permit communication.
subfiles.summary: Foreign Service cover with file and routing stamps; substantive text is absent.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Brazil concerning Naji Tacla's family
subfiles.about: Reports issuance of United States transit visas to Naji Tacla, his wife, and child.
subfiles.summary: The Yokohama office issued the family transit visas after Tacla showed that Brazilian visas would be granted at San Francisco. State presumed Brazil had arranged their expenses and prompt onward departure.

subfiles.title: Action-copy routing sheet, first copy
subfiles.about: Blank action copy bearing file reference 894.111/3-1648.
subfiles.summary: Action-copy sheet without substantive correspondence.

subfiles.title: Action-copy routing sheet, second copy
subfiles.about: Second blank action copy bearing the same file reference.
subfiles.summary: Action-copy sheet without substantive correspondence.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Giacomo Mensace's Okinawa travel request
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Forwards a Shanghai request concerning Italian passport holder Giacomo Mensace.
subfiles.summary: The request sought permission for travel involving Okinawa; the military attaché reportedly had no objection, and State asked the Army for a decision.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting clarification of Mensace's Okinawa trip
subfiles.about: Asks what Mensace intends to do in Okinawa, including whether he seeks scrap for China.
subfiles.summary: SCAP requires a more specific explanation of the proposed trip's commercial purpose.

subfiles.title: Foreign Missions Conference letter on two Finnish missionaries
subfiles.from: Royal H. Fisher, Foreign Missions Conference of North America
subfiles.about: Reports progress securing clearances for two Finnish mission women awaiting travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Finnish mission's Tokyo representative approached the Swedish Embassy, and clearance was reportedly in hand. The women were advised to extend their United States stay while awaiting formal confirmation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Alfred Brookes's extension request
subfiles.about: Records National Cash Register's request for urgent handling of Brookes's extended theater clearance.
subfiles.summary: Thomas R. Taylor warned that Sydney's telegram was coming and asked for telephone notice when the Army replied.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting extended clearance for Alfred Brookes
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests an extension because transportation problems prevented Brookes from reaching Japan by March 30.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Army to consider a later entry period for Alfred Brookes.

subfiles.title: Transfer sheet for Iranian Embassy note
subfiles.about: Records transfer of an Iranian Embassy note concerning Houssein Mely.
subfiles.summary: The March 17 Iranian note was moved for indexing under another file number.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram cover sheet, file 894.111/3-1848
subfiles.about: Cover sheet for an incoming airgram.
subfiles.summary: No substantive message text survives on this page.

subfiles.title: Sydney airgram confirming Alfred Brookes's clearance
subfiles.about: Confirms Brookes's theater clearance for entry into Japan from April 1 through April 30.
subfiles.summary: The Sydney consul reports the new validity period requested for Alfred Brookes.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Albert Evan Small's military permit
subfiles.about: Records notice to Small that his military permit was valid April 15 through May 15.
subfiles.summary: Small accepted the dates, requested mailing to Nicholson File Company, and planned to sail from San Francisco aboard the SS Flying Dragon on April 2.

subfiles.title: Application of Albert Evan Small to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks to investigate restoration of Nicholson File Company's Japanese market and prewar connections.
subfiles.summary: Small describes the company's file-manufacturing business and plans to visit Yokohama, Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo, and Kyoto, as well as Seoul. The form notes his British passport and identifies Motozo Hayashi as a prewar Osaka contact.

subfiles.title: Nicholson File Company certification for Albert Evan Small
subfiles.from: Bruce R. Weiser, Nicholson File Company
subfiles.about: Certifies Small as the company's authorized Far Eastern representative.
subfiles.summary: Requests any possible assistance for Small's business mission.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Albert Evan Small's military permit
subfiles.about: Encloses Small's military permit and confirms waiver of the exit-permit requirement.
subfiles.summary: The permit allowed one return journey between April 15 and May 15; Small was asked to report any departure-plan changes.

subfiles.title: War Department routing sheet dated March 18
subfiles.about: War Department routing sheet associated with file 894.111/3-1848.
subfiles.summary: The page contains stamps and file references but no substantive text.

subfiles.title: War Department routing sheet dated March 22
subfiles.about: Second War Department routing sheet associated with the same file.
subfiles.summary: The page contains receipt stamps and no substantive correspondence.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on George Terk's military permit
subfiles.about: Notifies George Terk that his Japan permit was valid throughout April 1948.
subfiles.summary: Terk accepted the validity period and requested mailing to Alexander Terk Company in New York.

subfiles.title: Application of George Terk to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks commercial travel to expand the firm's trade in textiles, chinaware, and food products.
subfiles.summary: Terk planned to visit Tokyo, Osaka, Kobe, and Nagoya. The firm cited Alexander Terk's recent Japan trip and substantial recent Japanese purchases as reasons for sending another representative.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing George Terk's military permit
subfiles.about: Encloses an Army permit for a Japan journey between April 1 and April 30.
subfiles.summary: Terk is asked to report his exact departure details so State can waive exit-permit requirements.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on exit-permit waivers for aliens
subfiles.about: Records policy discussions concerning waivers for aliens traveling to Japan or Germany.
subfiles.summary: The Exit Permit Unit would routinely waive requirements for aliens endorsed by Protective Services. For Julius Mueller, State would request a waiver after receiving his exact departure date and port.

subfiles.title: Word Missionaries letter concerning Ponzelet and Thoneick
subfiles.about: Reports travel plans for two S.V.D. missionaries awaiting or using Japan military permits.
subfiles.summary: Johannes Ponzelet planned to sail May 21 aboard the SS General Gordon; Joseph Thoneick sailed March 12 aboard the SS General Meigs.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip, file 894.111/3-1648
subfiles.about: File-control card showing a charge and due date.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge slip with little legible substantive information.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip to O'Neill
subfiles.about: File-control card recording a charge to O'Neill.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge slip without substantive correspondence.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum concerning Julius Mueller's documentation
subfiles.about: Records Miss Delaney's questions about exit documents and a military permit for Julius Mueller.
subfiles.summary: Corkran initially offered Form AD-1 copies and explained that Mueller, a Swiss national, also needed an Army military permit for Japan.

subfiles.title: Application of Julius Mueller to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Describes Cosa Corporation's proposed exports to and imports from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mueller lists machine tools and industrial supplies for export and numerous Japanese consumer products for import. He proposes visiting Tokyo, Yokohama, Nagoya, Kyoto, Osaka, and Kobe.

subfiles.title: Cosa Corporation supporting letter for Julius Mueller
subfiles.about: Explains Cosa's Japanese corporate interests, machine-tool agencies, and Mueller's proposed April journey.
subfiles.summary: Mueller describes prewar interests in two Swiss companies operating in Japan, the firm's worldwide representation of American machine-tool manufacturers, and his plan to travel in early April and return at month's end.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Julius Mueller's military permit
subfiles.about: Encloses Mueller's permit and requests exact departure details for an exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: State asks Mueller to report when and where he will leave the United States.

subfiles.title: Speedletter to Miss Delaney on Mueller's exit documentation
subfiles.about: Explains waiver procedures for Swiss national Julius Mueller's departure to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Protective Services normally secured exit-permit waivers for aliens traveling on American business. Delaney should provide Mueller's exact departure details after his military permit arrived, and Corkran offered immediate telephone notice.

subfiles.title: United States Political Adviser for Japan routing cover
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Routing cover for an enclosure filed under 894.111/3-1948.
subfiles.summary: Cover contains office and filing stamps but no readable substantive message.

subfiles.title: Copy memorandum on payments to Japanese agents
subfiles.from: F. Pickell, Acting Chief, Foreign Trade Division
subfiles.about: Explains dollar payments and equivalent yen disbursements to agents through commercial banking channels.
subfiles.summary: Payments for an agent's services would be remitted in dollars or foreign exchange; the named Japanese organization would pay the agent in yen at the current military conversion rate.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting April permit validity for Mr. Adamson
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests a Japan military permit for Adamson covering the entire month of April.
subfiles.summary: State reports that Adamson is in Los Angeles and wants the permit's validity adjusted to his proposed travel.

subfiles.title: Action slip for entry and travel in occupied territories
subfiles.about: Administrative action slip concerning entry and travel in occupied territories.
subfiles.summary: The form is largely blank or illegible.

subfiles.title: Illegible letter fragment filed April 16
subfiles.about: Fragment of a closing and routing notation from a travel-permit letter.
subfiles.summary: Only a closing, New York reference, and filing date remain legible.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum clearing three Commerce representatives
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Reports clearance of Robert Liewer, Ezra D. Hazan, and M. J. Benuvar for Japan entry.
subfiles.summary: The representatives in Saigon, Hong Kong, and Manila could enter during April and remain sixty days. Each was required to carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Application for Ezra D. Hazan to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests Japan entry for Syrian textile expert Ezra D. Hazan, then waiting in Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Hazan had lived and traded in Japan before the war, was interned by Japan, and later released by the United States Army. His employer wanted him to expand purchases of Japanese textiles under the SCAP program.

subfiles.title: War Department routing sheet for cleared representatives
subfiles.about: Routes the Army clearance memorandum associated with file 894.111/3-2248.
subfiles.summary: War Department receipt sheet with entry-period and filing notations.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Buenos Aires on Argentine travel applications
subfiles.about: Advises how an Argentine applicant should seek permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Because Argentine interests in Japan were protected by another power, an applicant still in Argentina should use diplomatic channels; State could accept the application if he were already in Japan-related circumstances described in the message.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip, file 894.111
subfiles.about: Administrative charge slip for file 894.111.
subfiles.summary: The form contains only a file number and routing marks.

subfiles.title: Embassy of Burma routing cover
subfiles.about: Embassy routing cover filed under 894.111/3-2348.
subfiles.summary: The page contains chancery and filing stamps without readable substantive text.

subfiles.title: Royal Egyptian Embassy note concerning Isaac Cohen
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Asks American authorities to communicate Cohen's application to Tokyo and secure the necessary permit.
subfiles.summary: The Egyptian Embassy formally seeks United States assistance with Isaac Cohen's proposed journey to Japan.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary copy of Cohen's application enclosure
subfiles.about: Sparse fragment of a copied Japan-entry application or enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Only references to Japan, passport information, and the Foreign Affairs ministry in Cairo are legible.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding Isaac Cohen's application to the Army
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Forwards duplicate applications for Egyptian citizen Isaac Cohen and requests a SCAP decision.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Army to communicate Cohen's application to the Supreme Commander and report the result.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on procedures for Egyptian Japan applications
subfiles.about: Records State-Army discussions over whether Washington should process Isaac Cohen's application.
subfiles.summary: Captain Rawls argued that Egyptian travelers should apply through British channels because Britain protected Egyptian interests in Japan. Williams replied that Circular 8 still allowed exceptional American assistance. The Army accepted Cohen's already-submitted application but expected future third-power cases to be handled in Washington only when unusually urgent.

subfiles.title: Illegible outgoing airgram, file 894.111
subfiles.about: Outgoing airgram concerning a Japan travel matter; substantive text is illegible.
subfiles.summary: Only routing codes, office distributions, and the preparation date can be read.

subfiles.title: Blank outgoing telegram copy
subfiles.about: Copy form for an outgoing telegram.
subfiles.summary: No substantive telegram text is visible.

subfiles.title: Blank incoming telegram form
subfiles.about: Incoming telegram form without readable message text.
subfiles.summary: Only the form heading and file marking are present.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum on Y. I. E. Assia's military permit
subfiles.about: Records Assia's inquiry about his military permit to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Corkran confirmed that the permit allowed entry from April 1 through April 30, and Assia requested delivery to his company's New York office.
